Magnachip Semiconductor.why: pure-play power semiconductor maker whose new MV SGT MOSFETs (server PSU synchronous rectification) and 600V SJ MOSFETs are designed for AI server and data-center power supplies
Magnachip Semiconductor.evidence: Magnachip Semiconductor press release (06-23-2026): two new 6th-generation 600V Super Junction MOSFETs designed for AI server power applications; (03-31-2026) 8th-generation 40V/60V MV MOSFETs for server PSU synchronous rectification

players.product: power MOSFETs for AI server / data-center power supplies (8th-gen 40V/60V MV SGT MOSFETs for PSU synchronous rectification, 6th-gen 600V SJ MOSFETs), plus IGBTs and licensed SiC technology

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 (CFO Shinyoung Park): consolidated revenue from continuing operations (Power Analog Solutions and Power IC) $44.7 million, within guidance of $44.5 million-$48.5 million; down 6.1% year-over-year and 3.3% sequentially - the year-over-year decline from weaker legacy-product demand due to intensified pricing competition, the sequential decline from seasonal softness in communication. Gross margin 19.3%, above the 17%-19% guidance range; R&D $7.9 million on new generation product development; adjusted EBITDA negative $4.2 million.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $44.7 million (-6.1% Y/Y, -3.3% Q/Q); gross margin 19.3%

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 guidance (CFO): revenue from continuing operations $41.5 million-$45.5 million (down 2.7% sequentially and 5.2% year-over-year at the midpoint), gross margin 17%-19%; the planned electrical substation upgrade lowers Q3 fab utilization, so Q4 gross margin is expected to decline slightly from Q3. Remains on track for its target of 55 new generation products in 2026, and continues to expect new generation products to contribute at least 10% of revenue in 'full quarter of 2026' (as transcribed) versus approximately 2% for full year 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue $41.5 million-$45.5 million; gross margin 17%-19%; 55 new generation products in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: CFO on Q3 headwinds: demand for its Low Voltage Battery FET line for mobile remains healthy, but Q3 revenue is expected to decline on packaging constraints in its supply chain that limit its ability to fully satisfy demand, lower customer volumes in certain custom applications, and an unfavorable mix from continued pricing pressure on legacy products.

Navitas partnership (CEO Chae Lee): Magnachip will license Navitas' silicon carbide technology covering 1200 volt, 2300 volt, 3300 volt and higher-voltage applications and gain access to its established silicon carbide supply chain ecosystem; it plans to qualify and ultimately manufacture those products in its fab in Korea, targeting energy and grid infrastructure, industrial electrification, automotive, renewable energy and other high-power applications. CEO: it combines Navitas' silicon carbide technology with Magnachip's silicon IGBT and MOSFET technologies.
quarterly_data.figure: 1200 V / 2300 V / 3300 V SiC technology licence

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Chae Lee (first call as CEO): Magnachip is repositioning as a pure-play power semiconductor company and aims to move from follower to leader by competing on differentiated, application-specific products rather than price, since much of the legacy power semiconductor market has become commoditized; Q2 reflected heavy dependence on legacy products, but recently introduced new generation products carrying higher margins are starting to show strength.
